I spent the early morning at our neighborhood farmer markets again this week. There's a small vendor with fresh vegetables every week that I hadn' noticed in all that I visited, selling produce and homemade jam from a small cooler on the street. It's not uncommon in the market. The jam was priced a fraction less, the flavors were intriguing - I'd seen some of it at a friend 'house. So today when it appeared at its regular slot, with an abundance this week - it felt as though a reminder had appeared for the day.
I had forgotten how good it tastes on toast with fresh honey butter and salted sea-fine cracked black-peper, but now the memory had stirred.
The jam had the right consistency with enough texture to stand-up, and the taste of the fresh raspberrie with just a slight under-tickness,
